fullPassage:
The Magic of Morning Pages

Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is Regan, your podcast host. Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people, including me, find enormously useful. It's a kind of journaling called "the morning pages." There is no age at which it is too late to form this habit. I started eight years ago as a high school student, and that's why today's episode is especially for my teenage subscribers.

The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life.

There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.

Now, let me share the experiences of some people I interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager, who has been writing morning pages for two years, says:

My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more productive.

Now, let's listen to Yuna, a high school junior:

When I started this exercise last year, I simply wrote random thoughts like this:
I'm sleepy. A slight headache's starting.
I need to finish the math assignment today …
I don't know what more to write now.

But soon I found I had deeper and deeper thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about today's tasks or worries. After that, I write about my dreams and how to move towards them. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I'm much happier than before.

I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life!

Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" "Why are things less fun these days?" Then, I started raising more challenging ones: "What could make me happier right now?" "What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?"

Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I've also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the drive and ideas to achieve these aims.

Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve your mental health and help you lead a happier, more creative life.

❌ ④ 해당 없음
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형/to부정사. help + O + -ing는 불가. help overcome / help to overcome 가능

det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ② concentrating: it wasn't easy for me to concentrate — 가주어 it + to부정사 구문
❌ ① mine: 소유대명사, my experiences 대신. 올바름
❌ ③ writing: try + -ing(시도해 보다). 올바름
❌ ④ changed: 과거시제. 올바름
det.tip: It is + 형용사 + for + 사람 + to부정사. -ing 형태 불가. try + -ing = 시도해 보다, try + to = ~하려고 노력하다

det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ has: 주어 My morning pages(복수) → have given. 관계절 삽입에 의한 주어-동사 수일치 혼동
❌ ① which: 계속적 용법 관계대명사, 앞 문장을 선행사로. 올바름
❌ ② what: 간접의문문 what kind of person. 올바름
❌ ③ being: 전치사 of + 동명사. 올바름
det.tip: 삽입절(관계절)이 주어와 동사 사이에 오면 수일치 혼동. pages(복수) → have

❌ ③ productive(생산적인): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ purpose(목적의식): 원문 그대로

✅ 정답 ② damaged: 원문은 improved(향상시켰다). 내적 평화 → 학업 향상의 긍정 맥락에 damaged 부적절

❌ ③ 다른 사람에게 보여주기: completely private 반대

ch: 집중력 향상 → 감정 해소 → 내적 평화
학업 향상 → 내적 평화 → 감정 해소
감정 해소 → 내적 평화 → 학업 향상

det.analysis:
✅ ③ 감정 해소 → 내적 평화 → 학업 향상: 원문의 인과관계 그대로

❌ ② 학업 향상이 먼저: 학업 향상은 결과
❌ ④ 내적 평화가 먼저: 감정 해소가 먼저
det.tip: 인과관계: releasing feelings → relieve tension → inner peace → improved performance

det.korean: these questions = 앞에서 언급된 'more challenging ones' = 자기 자신에 대한 도전적인 질문들 (예: '무엇이 나를 행복하게 만들까?')
det.analysis:
✅ ② 자기 자신에 대한 도전적인 질문들: 앞 문장의 'more challenging ones' 참조
❌ ① 학교 시험: 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ David의 레시피: David의 질문과 다름
❌ ④ 인터뷰 질문: Regan이 자신에게 한 질문
det.tip: these questions = 'What could make me happier?' 'What is my ideal future?' 등 자기 성찰적 질문

questions.passage: I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life!
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"Regan은 처음 매일 세 쪽 글쓰기를 시도했을 때, 그것을 __________ 것이라 기대하지 않았다."

(**영어** 단어를 쓰시오. 두 단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'I didn't expect to stick to it' — 계속할(stick to) 것이라 기대하지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ stick to: 원문에서 직접 찾기. 'expect to stick to it'
det.tip: stick to = ~을 고수하다, 계속하다. stick-stuck-stuck

questions.passage: Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"Regan은 자기 질문에 답하면서 자신의 필요, 가치, 열정, 그리고 __________이 무엇인지 알게 되었다."

(**영어** 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'my needs, values, passions, and talents' — 재능.
det.analysis: ✅ talents: 원문에서 직접 찾기. needs, values, passions, and talents
det.tip: talent(재능). 복수형 talents 주의. 4가지 나열: needs, values, passions, talents

questions.passage: Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? __________. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again!
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어들을 올바른 순서로 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.

[you / what / energy / you / creative / have / know / never / until / or / ideas / start / exploring]

(모든 단어를 사용할 것, 대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
questions.wa: You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring
accept: You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring
you never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring
You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring.
you never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring.

det.korean: 탐험을 시작해 보기 전에는 여러분이 어떤 창조적 에너지나 아이디어를 갖고 있는지 결코 알 수 없다.
det.analysis: ✅ You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring: 원문 그대로
det.tip: You never know ~ until ...: ~하기 전까지는 결코 알 수 없다. not ~ until 구문

questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of free writing, ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity.
questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.

"마음에 떠오르는 것은 무엇이든 쓰세요."

→ Write __________ crosses your mind.

(복합관계대명사를 사용할 것)

det.korean: 원문: 'write whatever crosses your mind' — 마음에 떠오르는 것은 무엇이든.
det.analysis: ✅ whatever: 복합관계대명사. '~하는 것은 무엇이든'
det.tip: whatever = anything that. whatever crosses your mind = 마음에 떠오르는 것은 무엇이든

questions.passage: I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I have also published a book and a music album. My morning pages have given me the motivation and ideas to achieve these aims.
questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.

"나의 모닝페이지는 나에게 이런 목표들을 달성하기 위한 추진력과 아이디어들을 주었다."

→ My morning pages have given me the __________ and ideas to achieve these aims.

(한 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'have given me the drive and ideas' — 추진력과 아이디어.
det.analysis: ✅ drive: 원문에서 직접 찾기. drive = 추진력/동기
det.tip: drive(추진력) — 목표를 향해 나아가게 하는 내적 동기. give someone the drive = ~에게 추진력을 주다
